title: Salt Block and Camera Placement Restrictions
abstract: Operational restrictions following unsuccessful attempts to photograph the Lantern Ridge animal with wildlife lures.
subject: Salt Block and Camera Placement Restrictions

body.text: Discontinue placement of mineral blocks within 100 meters of the mile 48 culvert. The blocks attract ordinary elk to the highway shoulder, interfere with track comparison, and create a traffic hazard unrelated to the reported animal.

Two blocks placed near the west exit were consumed overnight without tracks, tooth marks, fragments, or disturbance of the snow. This absence does not justify additional blocks. A missing lure is not improved by increasing the quantity of missing lure.

body.label: Camera placement
body.text: Mount cameras outside the traveled shoulder and aim them away from oncoming traffic. Do not place a camera inside the culvert. The pipe is active drainage infrastructure, not a blind, den entrance, or personnel shelter.

Wildlife officers may continue ordinary seasonal surveys. Reports should use “unidentified cervid” or the case number. “Long elk” is acceptable in quoted witness statements but should not be entered as a species in harvest, collision, or feed-allocation databases.
